docs.title: Harbor Resource Operator
docs.text:
The Harbor Resource Operator manages configuration inside a running Harbor registry as Kubernetes resources. You declare projects, robot accounts, replication endpoints and policies, project members, labels, immutable tag rules, webhooks, tag retention and the garbage collection schedule in YAML, and the operator keeps Harbor in line with them.

It does not install or upgrade Harbor; use the Harbor Helm chart for that. The operator talks to Harbor's REST API v2.0 only and depends on no other operator.

  • Install: Helm, a single manifest, or OperatorHub.
  • Quick start: connect a Harbor and create a project with a robot account.
  • How it behaves: managed fields, drift correction, adoption, deletion.
  • Reference: every field of the eleven kinds.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• Harbor as code. Projects, quotas, robot accounts and replication live in Git next to the workloads that use them, and Argo CD or Flux apply them like any other manifest.
  • Pull secrets that look after themselves. A HarborRobotAccount writes its credentials to a Secret (kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson if you like), refreshes it if it is lost and rotates it before the robot expires.
  • No drift. The operator re-reads Harbor on a sync period and restores what you declared, with a DriftCorrected event.
  • Safe by default. Projects are kept when their Kubernetes object is deleted, and never deleted while they still hold repositories.

docs.title: Kinds
docs.text: Kind What it manages HarborConnection URL and credentials of one Harbor; which namespaces may use it HarborProject Project, public flag, storage quota, scan metadata, CVE allowlist, proxy cache HarborRobotAccount Project or system robot with permissions; credentials in a Secret; rotation HarborRegistry Replication endpoint (another Harbor, ECR, Docker Hub, ...) HarborReplicationPolicy Push or pull replication with filters and trigger; the latest execution HarborProjectMember A user or an LDAP, HTTP or OIDC group with a project role HarborLabel Global or project label HarborImmutableRule Immutable tag rule HarborWebhook Project webhook policy with HTTP or Slack targets HarborRetentionPolicy Tag retention rules and schedule HarborGarbageCollection The system garbage collection schedule; the last run

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
Tested Harbor 2.12, 2.13, 2.14, 2.15 (end-to-end with the official chart: 2.15 on every push, all four nightly) Kubernetes 1.30 and later: 1.30, 1.34 and 1.37 end-to-end on kind, 1.37 envtest OpenShift not tested yet; the pod meets the restricted Pod Security Standard Architectures linux/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/s390x, linux/ppc64le

The API is v1alpha1: all eleven kinds are implemented and tested, and changes inside v1alpha1 are additive where possible.

Note

This is an independent community project, maintained by Oreon IT. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Harbor project or the CNCF; Harbor is a trademark of The Linux Foundation.

docs.title: Publishing on OperatorHub
docs.text: How the operator is packaged for Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) and listed on OperatorHub. This is milestone 3 item D2 (see REQUIREMENTS.md section 14). The catalog rules below were checked against the community-operators and operator-pipelines docs on 2026-11-01; check them again before each first-of-its-kind submission, because both repositories change their process from time to time.

docs.title: 1. Where the operator gets listed
docs.text:
Catalog Repository Seen in Tested by their CI on OperatorHub.io (upstream Kubernetes) k8s-operatorhub/community-operators operatorhub.io, the quay.io/operatorhubio/catalog index, Artifact Hub kind/minikube OpenShift and OKD embedded OperatorHub redhat-openshift-ecosystem/community-operators-prod the OpenShift console, registry.redhat.io/redhat/community-operator-index:v4.x an OpenShift 4 cluster

The two catalogs are separate, with one pull request to each for every release. A listing on OperatorHub.io does not show up on OpenShift. The certified and Red Hat Marketplace catalogs are a different programme and out of scope.

Order: OperatorHub.io first (its CI matches what we test on), then OpenShift once a release has run on a real OpenShift cluster.

docs.title: 2. How the bundle is built
docs.text:
operator-sdk is used as a build tool only; the operator has no SDK code. make operator-sdk downloads the pinned release into bin/.

Path What it is config/manifests/bases/harbor-resource-operator.clusterserviceversion.yaml CSV base: tile text, description, icon, keywords, links, maintainers, install modes, minKubeVersion, capability level. Written by hand; operator-sdk generate kustomize manifests keeps it and only refreshes the owned CRD list. config/manifests/kustomization.yaml Input for make bundle: config/default, the samples and the scorecard config. config/manifests/samples/ config/samples with the Secrets removed. The bundle must not ship credentials, and alm-examples only lists custom resources. The CSV description names the Secrets users create. config/scorecard/ Scorecard tests (basic and OLM suites). docs/images/icon.svg The project's own icon, embedded in the CSV. It is not the Harbor logo. bundle/, bundle.Dockerfile Generated by make bundle; committed for each release, and copied as-is into the catalog repositories.

Targets:

make bundle            # regenerate bundle/ for VERSION (channel alpha) and run the basic validation
make bundle-validate   # the checks OperatorHub runs (suite=operatorframework)
make bundle-build      # bundle image BUNDLE_IMG (default ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-resource-operator-bundle:vVERSION)
make bundle-push

USE_IMAGE_DIGESTS=true make bundle pins the manager image by digest and fills spec.relatedImages, which disconnected OpenShift clusters need. It is off for now, so the CSV says features.operators.openshift.io/disconnected: "false".

On a vX.Y.Z tag (created by tag-release.yml when main gets a new VERSION) the release workflow checks that the committed bundle/ is for X.Y.Z, runs make bundle-validate, pushes and signs the bundle image, and attaches harbor-resource-operator-bundle-X.Y.Z.tgz to the GitHub release.

docs.title: Validation result
docs.text: make bundle-validate passes. It prints one warning, which is a false positive: the events.k8s.io events rule in the CSV is reported as "deprecated and removed in v1.25". What was removed in 1.25 is events.k8s.io/v1beta1; the operator uses events.k8s.io/v1, but RBAC rules carry no API version, so the validator flags the group. Removing the rule would break event recording.

It was 1.34.0 up to 0.1.3, which failed the OperatorHub.io kiwi test: that job runs kind with Kubernetes 1.30, so OLM never created the Deployment. Lower it only together with the nightly job maturity, channel alpha, default channel alpha add a stable channel when the API reaches v1beta1 or v1 provider Oreon IT, https://www.oreonit.com the company that maintains the project. The listing shows the name as plain text and does not link provider.url, so the site is also in links maintainers Fahri Cap, fahri.cap@oreonit.com links, support GitHub repository, README, issues, the Harbor Helm chart, Oreon IT there is no separate docs site yet; switch Documentation when there is arch labels amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x, linux the release image is built for these OpenShift feature annotations proxy-aware: "true", everything else "false" the Harbor transport clones Go's default transport, so it reads HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY; confirm once on a proxied cluster

Descriptors and resources come from // +operator-sdk:csv:customresourcedefinitions:... markers in api/v1alpha1: one on each kind (display name and the resources it uses) and one on each top-level spec field and on status.conditions. Add the marker when adding a spec field, or the scorecard's olm-spec-descriptors test fails. The kind marker must stay inside the +kubebuilder marker block; a blank line between them makes controller-gen drop the short names, printer columns and status subresource.

docs.title: 4. Before the first submission
docs.text:
1. Make the bundle image public. After the first release that pushes it, set harbor-resource-operator-bundle on ghcr.io to public, like the operator image and the chart. The catalog CI pulls the manager image anonymously; the bundle image is only for our own tests and operator-sdk run bundle.
  2. Install test with OLM on kind. Install OLM (operator-sdk olm install), build and push a bundle image somewhere the cluster can pull from, then operator-sdk run bundle <bundle image> --namespace operators. Check that the CSV reaches Succeeded, the manager Deployment is available, and a HarborConnection to a real Harbor becomes Ready. Then run operator-sdk scorecard <bundle image>; the basic and OLM suites must all pass. Clean up with operator-sdk cleanup harbor-resource-operator. This catches RBAC that works with kustomize but is missing from the CSV.
  3. Version. v0.1.0 was released before the bundle existed, so it has no bundle image or archive. The first submission is 0.1.2, the first release with the final provider listing (0.1.1 had a placeholder provider).

docs.title: 5. Submitting a release to OperatorHub.io
docs.text:
This stays manual: a release is not on OperatorHub until someone submits it, and not every release needs to be. Submit after the GitHub release of X.Y.Z is green.

  1. Check the bundle. minKubeVersion in the CSV must be at or below the Kubernetes version of their kind test (1.30 at the time of writing, see upstream/local.yml in operator-test-playbooks), or the install test never starts the Deployment.
  2. Upgrade test from the version currently listed, as in section 6.
  3. Copy the bundle into a branch of your fork of k8s-operatorhub/community-operators, cut from its current main: 
    git -C community-operators fetch upstream && git -C community-operators switch -c harbor-resource-operator-X.Y.Z upstream/main
mkdir -p community-operators/operators/harbor-resource-operator/X.Y.Z
cp -r bundle/manifests bundle/metadata community-operators/operators/harbor-resource-operator/X.Y.Z/
    (or unpack harbor-resource-operator-bundle-X.Y.Z.tgz from the GitHub release). Leave tests/scorecard out. ci.yaml is already there: 
    reviewers:
  - fahricap
updateGraph: semver-mode
    With semver-mode the CSV needs no spec.replaces; OLM orders versions by semver, and skipped versions are fine.
  4. Commit with a DCO sign-off whose name and e-mail match the author (git commit -s -m "operator harbor-resource-operator (X.Y.Z)"), one operator version per pull request, push, and open the pull request against their main. In the description, say what changed against the listed version and how it was tested.
  5. Their CI validates the bundle, installs it on kind and checks that the Deployment becomes healthy. Results are in the Checks tab; /retest reruns them. With the author in reviewers, a green run merges the pull request automatically; the listing updates on operatorhub.io after their release pipeline runs.
  6. Record it in the status table below. Published versions are never edited; fixes go out as a new version.

docs.title: 6. Upgrade test (from the second release on)
docs.text: operator-sdk run bundle the previous bundle image, create objects and wait for Ready, then operator-sdk run bundle-upgrade to the new one, and check that the objects stay Ready with their Harbor IDs kept. Add this to CI before claiming level 2 for a release that changes the CRDs.

docs.title: 7. Submitting to OpenShift (community-operators-prod)
docs.text:
Same bundle directory, pull request rules and reviewers, with two differences:

  • Tested on OpenShift. Their CI deploys the bundle on an OpenShift 4 cluster. Run it once on OpenShift Local (CRC) or OKD first: check that the pod is admitted under restricted-v2 (it sets no fixed UID), that the metrics Service works with OpenShift monitoring, and that the operator reaches a Harbor route with a cluster-signed CA.
  • File-based catalog (FBC). New operators are expected to use FBC. ci.yaml gets: 
    reviewers:
  - fahricap
fbc:
  enabled: true
  catalog_mapping:
    - template_name: semver.yaml
      catalogs_names: ["v4.16", "v4.17", "v4.18", "v4.19", "v4.20"]
      type: olm.semver
    Next to it go catalog-templates/semver.yaml and their FBC Makefile (make catalogs renders catalogs/v4.x/harbor-resource-operator/catalog.yaml with opm). Each release is two pull requests: the bundle, then the catalog update with the bundle pullspec their pipeline comments. Their auto-release option opens the second one automatically. Check the OpenShift versions currently served before writing catalogs_names, and add com.redhat.openshift.versions (for example "v4.16") to bundle/metadata/annotations.yaml in that copy.

docs.title: Harbor Resource Operator: requirements
docs.text: Version 0.1, 2026-11-01. Status: milestones 1 and 2 are implemented and covered by unit, envtest and end-to-end tests against Harbor 2.12 to 2.15. Milestone 3 (distribution) is in progress.

docs.title: 1. Purpose and positioning
docs.text:
A Kubernetes operator that manages configuration inside a running Harbor registry (projects, robot accounts, replication endpoints and policies, later retention, immutability, webhooks, members, labels) as Kubernetes resources, so that registry configuration lives in Git next to the workloads that use it.

It deliberately does not deploy or upgrade Harbor itself. Harbor's own Helm chart does that and is maintained by the Harbor team. The archived official operator was hard to maintain because it re-implemented the chart in Go for every Harbor component and embedded three third-party operators; this project is the opposite shape: one bounded job against Harbor's versioned REST API v2.0, no third-party operators, no conversion webhooks in v1alpha1.

docs.title: 2. Goals
docs.text:
• G1. Declarative, idempotent management of Harbor resources from any namespace, against one or many Harbor instances.
  • G2. Drift correction: if someone changes a managed field in the Harbor UI, the operator restores the declared value on the next sync.
  • G3. Robot account credentials delivered to workloads as Kubernetes Secrets, including ready-to-use image pull secrets, with rotation.
  • G4. Safe by default: nothing in Harbor is deleted unless the resource says so; projects are retained on deletion by default.
  • G5. Small and bounded enough for a single maintainer to keep current with Kubernetes and Harbor releases.
  • G6. Works on upstream Kubernetes and OpenShift, installable by Helm or OLM.

docs.title: 3. Non-goals
docs.text:
• Installing, upgrading, backing up or scaling Harbor (use the Harbor Helm chart).
  • Managing Harbor users, LDAP/OIDC settings or system configuration (except garbage collection schedule in milestone 2).
  • Mirroring image contents, scanning, or acting on vulnerability reports.
  • Multi-cluster federation of resources.
  • A web UI.

docs.title: 4. Users and use cases
docs.text: User Use case Platform engineer Creates a HarborProject per team via GitOps (Argo CD or Flux) with quota, auto-scan and public flag; teams get a project without a ticket Application team Declares a HarborRobotAccount with pull permission on their project; the operator writes an image pull Secret the Deployment references CI/CD owner Declares a push robot for the pipeline namespace with a 90-day duration and automatic rotation; the Secret is updated in place Multi-site operator Declares HarborRegistry endpoints (a second Harbor, ECR, Docker Hub) and HarborReplicationPolicy objects to push releases to edge sites on a schedule Compliance owner (milestone 2) Declares retention and immutability rules per project, and a webhook to the SIEM, as code MSP or consultancy Points one operator at several customer Harbors through separate HarborConnection objects with namespace restrictions

docs.title: 5. Scope by milestone
docs.text: Milestone Kinds Deliverables M1 (core) HarborConnection, HarborProject, HarborRobotAccount, HarborRegistry, HarborReplicationPolicy Controllers with adoption, drift correction, deletion policies, conditions, events, metrics; unit tests with a fake Harbor; envtest suite; Helm chart; multi-arch image M2 (compliance) HarborRetentionPolicy, HarborImmutableRule, HarborWebhook, HarborProjectMember, HarborLabel, HarborGarbageCollection Same quality bar; e2e on kind with the Harbor chart in nightly CI M3 (distribution) none OLM bundle, OperatorHub and OpenShift community PRs, Artifact Hub, docs site, example repository for Argo CD and Flux, release automation, SBOM and signed images

docs.title: 6. API design
docs.text: API group harbor.oreonit.com, version v1alpha1. All kinds are namespaced. Field names follow Kubernetes conventions (camelCase), not Harbor's snake_case. Every kind has spec.connectionRef, spec.deletionPolicy, spec.adoptExisting, and a status with conditions, observedGeneration, and the Harbor-side identifier.

docs.title: 6.1 HarborConnection
docs.text:
Holds the URL and credentials of one Harbor instance.

apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborConnection
metadata:
  name: prod-harbor
  namespace: harbor-system
spec:
  url: https://harbor.example.com
  credentialsSecretRef:          # keys: username, password (admin or a system robot with enough permissions)
    name: prod-harbor-admin
  caBundleSecretRef:             # optional, key: ca.crt
    name: prod-harbor-ca
  insecureSkipTLSVerify: false
  allowedNamespaces: ["*"]       # namespaces whose resources may reference this connection; default: own namespace only
  syncPeriod: 10m                # default resync for resources using this connection
status:
  harborVersion: v2.14.6
  conditions:
  - type: Ready
    status: "True"
    reason: Connected

Requirements: - C1. The operator verifies the connection by calling GET /systeminfo and GET /users/current and reports the Harbor version and the authenticated account in status. - C2. Resources in other namespaces may reference the connection only if their namespace matches allowedNamespaces (exact names or *). A disallowed reference sets condition Ready=False, reason=ConnectionNotAllowed and does nothing in Harbor. - C3. Credentials are read at reconcile time, never cached across reconciles, never logged. - C4. A broken connection marks dependent resources Ready=False, reason=ConnectionUnavailable and retries with exponential backoff capped at the sync period.

docs.title: 6.2 HarborProject
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborProject
metadata:
  name: team-payments
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef: { name: prod-harbor, namespace: harbor-system }
  name: payments                  # Harbor project name; defaults to metadata.name
  public: false
  storageQuotaBytes: 53687091200  # optional; -1 for unlimited
  metadata:
    autoScan: true
    autoSbomGeneration: false
    preventVulnerable: true
    severity: critical            # none, low, medium, high, critical
    enableContentTrustCosign: false
    reuseSystemCVEAllowlist: true
  cveAllowlist:                   # optional
    expiresAt: "2027-01-31T00:00:00Z"
    items: ["CVE-2025-1234"]
  proxyCache:                     # optional; makes this a proxy cache project
    registryRef: { name: dockerhub-upstream }
  adoptExisting: false
  deletionPolicy: Retain          # Retain | Delete; default Retain
status:
  projectID: 42
  conditions: [...]

Requirements: - P1. Create via POST /projects; look up by name with HEAD /projects?project_name=; update via PUT /projects/{id} and quota via PUT /quotas/{id}. - P2. registryRef (proxy cache) is immutable after creation, as in Harbor; a change sets Ready=False, reason=ImmutableField. - P3. On deletionPolicy: Delete, call GET /projects/{id}/_deletable first; if Harbor says the project is not deletable (it has repositories), keep the finalizer, set condition Deleting=False, reason=ProjectNotEmpty, emit a warning event, and retry on the sync period. Never delete repositories. - P4. Only fields set in spec are managed. Unset optional fields are left as Harbor has them.

docs.title: 6.3 HarborRobotAccount
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborRobotAccount
metadata:
  name: payments-ci
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef: { name: prod-harbor, namespace: harbor-system }
  name: payments-ci               # Harbor adds the robot$ prefix (and project+ for project-level)
  level: project                  # project | system
  projectRef: { name: team-payments }   # required for level: project (a HarborProject in this namespace) or use projectName
  description: CI pipeline push
  duration: 90                    # days; -1 never expires
  permissions:                    # for level: system, one entry per project namespace, or namespace "*"
  - namespace: payments
    access:
    - { resource: repository, action: push }
    - { resource: repository, action: pull }
    - { resource: artifact, action: read }
  secret:
    name: payments-ci-robot       # default <metadata.name>-robot
    type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson   # or Opaque (keys: username, password, host)
    labels: {}
    annotations: {}
  rotation:
    period: 30d                   # optional; refreshes the secret via PATCH /robots/{id}
    beforeExpiry: 7d              # optional; rotate when expires_at is near
  disabled: false
  adoptExisting: false
  deletionPolicy: Delete
status:
  robotID: 17
  robotName: robot$payments+payments-ci
  expiresAt: "2027-01-29T10:00:00Z"
  lastRotation: "2026-10-31T10:00:00Z"
  secretRef: { name: payments-ci-robot }
  conditions: [...]

Requirements: - R1. Harbor returns the robot secret only at creation (POST /robots) or refresh (PATCH /robots/{id}). The operator stores it in the Kubernetes Secret immediately and never in status, logs or events. - R2. If the Secret is missing or lacks the password key on a later reconcile, the operator refreshes the robot secret and rewrites the Secret, and emits an event SecretRecreated. - R3. Permissions are reconciled via PUT /robots/{id}; name, level and project are immutable (Harbor behaviour). - R4. Adoption of an existing robot requires adoptExisting: true and triggers a secret refresh, because the existing secret is unknown; this is documented as rotating the credential. - R5. For kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, the registry host is derived from the connection URL and the Secret carries an annotation with the robot name and expiry for humans. - R6. The Secret is owned by the HarborRobotAccount (owner reference) and removed with it; deletionPolicy: Retain keeps the robot in Harbor but still removes the Secret.

docs.title: 6.4 HarborRegistry (replication endpoint)
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborRegistry
metadata:
  name: edge-eu-west
  namespace: platform
spec:
  connectionRef: { name: prod-harbor, namespace: harbor-system }
  name: edge-eu-west
  type: harbor                    # harbor, docker-hub, docker-registry, aws-ecr, azure-acr, google-gcr, github-ghcr, quay, ... (Harbor's list)
  url: https://harbor.eu-west.example.com
  insecure: false
  credentialsSecretRef:           # optional; keys: accessKey, accessSecret
    name: edge-eu-west-creds
  credentialType: basic           # basic | oauth
  description: Edge site EU West
  adoptExisting: false
  deletionPolicy: Delete
status:
  registryID: 3
  health: healthy
  conditions: [...]

Requirements: - E1. Before create or update, call POST /registries/ping; a failed ping sets Ready=False, reason=PingFailed with the Harbor message and still creates the registry only if spec.createEvenIfUnhealthy: true. - E2. Status reports Harbor's registry status field on every sync.

docs.title: 6.5 HarborReplicationPolicy
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborReplicationPolicy
metadata:
  name: releases-to-edge
  namespace: platform
spec:
  connectionRef: { name: prod-harbor, namespace: harbor-system }
  name: releases-to-edge
  direction: push                 # push: local -> destRegistryRef; pull: srcRegistryRef -> local
  destRegistryRef: { name: edge-eu-west }
  destNamespace: payments
  destNamespaceReplaceCount: -1
  filters:
  - { type: name, value: "payments/**" }
  - { type: tag, value: "v*" }
  - { type: resource, value: image }
  trigger:
    type: scheduled               # manual | scheduled | event_based
    cron: "0 0 2 * * *"
  override: true
  enabled: true
  replicateDeletion: false
  copyByChunk: false
  singleActiveReplication: true
  speedKBps: 0
  executeOnCreate: false          # POST /replication/executions once after creation
  adoptExisting: false
  deletionPolicy: Delete
status:
  policyID: 9
  lastExecution: { id: 120, status: Succeeded, startTime: ..., endTime: ... }
  conditions: [...]

Requirements: - S1. The referenced HarborRegistry must be Ready and belong to the same connection; otherwise Ready=False, reason=RegistryNotReady. - S2. Status mirrors the latest execution from GET /replication/executions?policy_id=. - S3. Filters and trigger are reconciled in full (the whole list is declared).

docs.title: 6.6 Milestone 2 kinds
docs.text:
All project-scoped kinds take exactly one of projectRef (a HarborProject in the same namespace, on the same connection) or projectName (an existing Harbor project). Both the project and, for members, the identity are immutable (CEL transition rules). They default to deletionPolicy: Delete.

  • HarborRetentionPolicy: rules[] (1 to 15) with template (latestPushedK, latestPulledN, nDaysSinceLastPush, nDaysSinceLastPull, always), count (required unless always), repositories and tags pattern selectors (tags.untagged, default true), disabled; schedule (six-field cron, empty for manual). Algorithm is always or. The policy is linked through the project's retention_id metadata; a stale pointer is cleared and a new policy created.
  • HarborImmutableRule: repositories and tags pattern selectors (decoration matches or excludes, doublestar pattern), disabled. Harbor has no rule name, so a rule is found by stored ID and otherwise by identical selectors. Harbor's priority field is not exposed and is kept as Harbor has it on update.
  • HarborWebhook: name, description, eventTypes[], targets[] (1 to 8; http or slack, address, authHeaderSecretRef, skipCertVerify, payloadFormat Default or CloudEvents), enabled. Secret changes trigger a reconcile; status keeps only the resourceVersions of the referenced Secrets, never their values.
  • HarborProjectMember: user (an existing Harbor user) or group (name, type ldap, http or oidc, ldapGroupDN), role (projectAdmin, maintainer, developer, guest, limitedGuest). Only the role is updated in place.
  • HarborLabel: name, color (#RRGGBB), description, scope: global | project (project needs a project reference).
  • HarborGarbageCollection: one effective object per connection (oldest wins, others report Duplicate); schedule (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, None or six-field cron), deleteUntagged, workers (1 to 5). Defaults to deletionPolicy: Retain; Delete sets the schedule to None. Status mirrors the next scheduled time and the last run.

docs.title: 7. Reconciliation semantics
docs.text:
• X1. Idempotent: every reconcile computes desired state from spec, reads actual state from Harbor by stored ID (status) or by name (first time), and applies the minimal update. No create when an ID is known; if the ID no longer exists in Harbor, the resource is recreated and an event RecreatedInHarbor is emitted.
  • X2. Adoption: if no ID is stored and an object with the same name exists in Harbor, adopt only when adoptExisting: true; otherwise set Ready=False, reason=AlreadyExists and do nothing.
  • X3. Managed fields: only fields present in spec are compared and written. This lets humans keep settings the spec does not mention.
  • X4. Drift correction runs on every sync period (default from the connection, overridable per resource with spec.syncPeriod) and on every spec change. Corrections emit a DriftCorrected event naming the field.
  • X5. Deletion: finalizer harbor.oreonit.com/finalizer. Retain removes the Kubernetes object and leaves Harbor untouched; Delete removes the Harbor object first, then the finalizer. Harbor 404 on delete counts as success.
  • X6. Ordering: a resource whose dependency (connection, project, registry) is not Ready requeues after 30 seconds without calling Harbor.
  • X7. Rate limiting: per-connection client with a token bucket (default 10 requests per second, burst 20) and a concurrency cap, so a large GitOps apply cannot overload Harbor.
  • X8. Status: conditions use metav1.Condition with types Ready, Synced, Deleting; observedGeneration is set on every status write. Status writes use the status subresource.
  • X9. Backoff: Harbor 5xx and network errors use controller-runtime's default exponential backoff; 4xx other than 404 and 409 do not retry until the spec changes (they are user errors) and are reported in the condition message.

docs.title: 8. Secrets and credentials
docs.text:
• K1. Connection credentials, registry credentials and webhook auth headers are read from Secrets by reference; the operator never embeds them in CRs.
  • K2. Robot secrets are written to Secrets the operator creates and owns; existing Secrets with the same name but no owner reference are not overwritten (condition SecretConflict).
  • K3. All Harbor API calls use HTTPS; insecureSkipTLSVerify is allowed but logged as a warning at startup and in the connection status.
  • K4. Logs redact Authorization headers and any field named secret, password, access_secret, auth_header.

docs.title: 9. Multi-tenancy and RBAC
docs.text:
• T1. Namespaced kinds; tenants manage resources in their namespaces; the connection owner controls which namespaces may use a connection (allowedNamespaces).
  • T2. The operator's own RBAC: get/list/watch on its kinds, update on status and finalizers, get/list/watch/create/update/delete Secrets it owns, create events. It needs no cluster-wide Secret read beyond that; referenced Secrets are read by name in the resource's own namespace (or the connection's namespace for connection credentials).
  • T3. Optional watch-namespace restriction via --watch-namespaces for single-tenant installs.

docs.title: 10. Observability
docs.text:
• O1. Prometheus metrics on the controller-runtime endpoint: reconcile counts and durations per kind (built in), plus harbor_api_requests_total{connection,method,code}, harbor_api_request_duration_seconds, harbor_resources{kind,connection,ready}, harbor_drift_corrections_total{kind}, harbor_robot_expiration_timestamp_seconds{namespace,name,robot} (Unix time of expiry, following the Prometheus _timestamp_seconds convention; alert with harbor_robot_expiration_timestamp_seconds - time() < 7*86400).
  • O2. Kubernetes events for create, update, drift correction, deletion, rotation, conflicts and Harbor errors.
  • O3. Structured JSON logs with resource keys; --zap-log-level as usual.
  • O4. kubectl get columns: Ready, Harbor ID, Age; robots also show Expires.

docs.title: 11. Compatibility
docs.text:
• V1. Harbor 2.12, 2.13, 2.14 and 2.15 tested end to end (2.15 on every push, all four nightly); API v2.0 only. New Harbor minors are added to the matrix within one month of release.
  • V2. Kubernetes 1.30 and later: end-to-end tested on 1.30 (nightly, the minimum), 1.34 and 1.37, envtest on 1.37. OpenShift: not yet tested; the pod meets the restricted Pod Security Standard (non-root, read-only filesystem, no capabilities, no fixed UID), which the restricted-v2 SCC requires.
  • V3. CRD schema changes within v1alpha1 are additive only; a v1beta1 with a conversion webhook is a milestone after M3 and only if the API has to change.

docs.title: 12. Non-functional
docs.text:
• N1. The operator runs as a single replica with leader election enabled for upgrades; a second replica is allowed.
  • N2. Resource usage under 100 MB memory and 0.1 CPU steady state for 1,000 managed resources.
  • N3. A full resync of 1,000 resources completes within 5 minutes under the default rate limit.
  • N4. Image: distroless, non-root, multi-arch (amd64, arm64, s390x, ppc64le), under 60 MB, SBOM attached, cosign-signed.

docs.title: 13. Testing
docs.text:
• Q1. Unit tests for the Harbor client against an httptest fake implementing the used endpoints, including error and pagination paths.
  • Q2. envtest suites per controller covering create, adopt, drift, delete with both policies, connection unavailable, and robot secret recreation.
  • Q3. End-to-end tests on kind with the Harbor Helm chart: the newest Harbor on every push, four Harbor minors nightly. They cover every kind, HTTPS with a custom CA, 300 objects on one rate-limited connection, metrics content and bulk deletion.
  • Q4. Lint (golangci-lint), go vet, govulncheck in CI; coverage target 70 percent for controllers and 90 percent for the client.

docs.title: 14. Packaging and distribution
docs.text:
• D1. Helm chart in-repo (charts/chart), published on each release to oci://ghcr.io/oreondev/charts/harbor-resource-operator, and listed on Artifact Hub.
  • D2. OLM bundle with CSV capability level "Seamless Upgrades" (level 2), spec.links to docs and source, spec.provider.url, icon; PRs to k8s-operatorhub/community-operators and the OpenShift community repository.
  • D3. Releases by semantic version from vX.Y.Z tags on main: GitHub Actions builds the multi-arch image, signs it with cosign (keyless), attaches SBOM and provenance, pushes image and chart to ghcr.io and creates a GitHub release with install.yaml. Renovate for dependency bumps.
  • D4. Repository name harbor-resource-operator to avoid confusion with the archived harbor-operator.

docs.title: 15. Documentation
docs.text: • A docs site, mirrored as README in the repository: install (Helm, OLM), connection setup with a least-privilege robot instead of admin, one page per kind with full field reference, GitOps examples for Argo CD and Flux, migration guide for adopting an existing Harbor, troubleshooting by condition reason.

docs.title: 16. Maintenance and ownership
docs.text: • Routine work: controller-runtime and Kubernetes dependency bumps with each Kubernetes minor (about every four months), Harbor minor compatibility runs, weekly issue triage. Harbor API v2.0 has been additive since 2.0 (2020); breaking changes are not expected inside 2.x.

docs.title: 17. Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Harbor changes robot or replication API semantics in a minor CI matrix across four Harbor versions; version-gated code paths if needed Admin credentials in a Secret are a high-value target Document and default to a system robot with only project/robot/registry/replication permissions; never require admin Users expect the operator to install Harbor Name, README first paragraph and OperatorHub description state the scope; link to the Harbor chart Accidental project deletion Retain default, _deletable check, no repository deletion ever Maintainer burnout Bounded scope, no third-party operators, no conversion webhooks in v1alpha1

docs.title: Appendix: Harbor API v2.0 endpoints used (from the 2.14.6 OpenAPI spec)
docs.text: Kind Endpoints Connection GET /systeminfo, GET /users/current Project HEAD /projects?project_name=, POST /projects, GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/{id}, GET /projects/{id}/_deletable, GET/PUT /quotas/{id} (quota found via GET /quotas?reference=project&reference_id=) RobotAccount GET /robots?q=name=, POST /robots, GET/PUT/DELETE /robots/{id}, PATCH /robots/{id} (secret refresh) Registry POST /registries/ping, GET /registries?q=name=, POST /registries, GET/PUT/DELETE /registries/{id} ReplicationPolicy GET /replication/policies?q=name=, POST /replication/policies, GET/PUT/DELETE /replication/policies/{id}, POST /replication/executions, GET /replication/executions?policy_id= M2

docs.title: Managed fields only
docs.text: Only fields you set in spec are managed. Fields you leave unset are left as Harbor has them, so you can adopt an existing project and manage just its quota.

docs.title: Drift correction
docs.text: Every syncPeriod (default 10 minutes, set on the connection or per resource) the operator re-reads Harbor and restores the declared values, emitting a DriftCorrected event. Objects deleted in Harbor behind its back are recreated.

docs.title: Finding and adopting objects
docs.text: The operator finds a Harbor object by the ID stored in status first, then by name. If an object of that name already exists in Harbor and was not created by this resource, the resource reports AlreadyExists and changes nothing until you set spec.adoptExisting: true. Adopting a robot account refreshes its secret, because Harbor never returns an existing secret.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text:
Every kind has deletionPolicy:

  • Delete removes the Harbor object when the Kubernetes object is deleted. A Harbor 404 counts as success.
  • Retain leaves it in Harbor.

HarborProject and HarborGarbageCollection default to Retain; the other kinds default to Delete. A project with Delete is only removed once it holds no repositories: until then the object stays with reason ProjectNotEmpty, and it is deleted as soon as the last repository is gone. The operator never deletes repositories or artifacts.

docs.title: Robot secrets
docs.text: Harbor only returns a robot secret when the robot is created. The operator writes it to the Secret immediately. If the Secret is deleted or loses its password, the robot secret is refreshed and the Secret rewritten. rotation.period refreshes on a schedule; rotation.beforeExpiry recreates the robot before it expires. Secrets never appear in status, events or logs.

docs.title: Multi-tenancy
docs.text: A resource may reference a connection in another namespace only if that connection lists the namespace (or *) in allowedNamespaces. Keep the credentials Secret in the connection's namespace and give application teams access only to their own namespaces.

docs.title: Project-scoped kinds
docs.text: Members, labels, immutable rules, webhooks, retention policies and project robots reference a HarborProject with projectRef (it must use the same connection), or name an existing Harbor project with projectName. The project and the member identity are immutable; recreate the object to change them.

docs.title: Rate limiting
docs.text: Each connection has one token bucket (requestsPerSecond, default 10) shared by all controllers, so a large GitOps sync does not overload Harbor.

docs.title: One garbage collection schedule per Harbor
docs.text: If several HarborGarbageCollection objects point at one connection, the oldest wins and the others report Duplicate.

docs.title: Status and events
docs.text: Every resource has a Ready condition with a reason (Synced, AlreadyExists, DependencyNotReady, ConnectionUnavailable, ProjectNotEmpty, ...) and a human-readable message, the Harbor ID in status, and Kubernetes events for creates, updates, adoption and drift corrections.

docs.title: Single-namespace installs
docs.text: --watch-namespaces=a,b restricts the manager cache, and so the operator, to those namespaces.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes are listed here, newest first. Versions follow semantic versioning; while the API is v1alpha1, a minor version may change it. Each release also has a GitHub release with the image digest and install files.

• Documentation site at https://www.oreonit.com/harbor-operator/, with a reference page for every kind generated from the CRDs and samples, and these release notes (#22).
  • pkg/harbor reads agent skills stored as OCI artifacts: ListArtifactsOfType (with signature accessories), and GetManifest and GetBlob on the registry API with digest and size checks. Artifacts carry artifact_type, annotations and extra_attrs. The fake Harbor serves /v2/ manifests and blobs and enforces the cosign pull policy. Used by the Harbor MCP server (#27).

docs.text: • Existing project robot accounts are found by name. Harbor's GET /robots lists only system robots unless the query names the project, so adoptExisting never worked for project robots, and a robot whose stored ID was lost failed on create instead of being found again (#16).

docs.title: Changed

docs.text: • The OLM bundle requires Kubernetes 1.30 or later (was 1.34). The end-to-end suite passes on Kubernetes 1.30 with Harbor 2.15, and the nightly run now covers 1.30 (#12).

  • Every kind and field has a description, shown by kubectl explain and on OperatorHub (#4).

First release.

  • Eleven kinds: HarborConnection, HarborProject, HarborRobotAccount, HarborRegistry, HarborReplicationPolicy, HarborProjectMember, HarborLabel, HarborImmutableRule, HarborWebhook, HarborRetentionPolicy and HarborGarbageCollection.

  • Tested end to end against Harbor 2.12, 2.13, 2.14 and 2.15.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The operator runs as one Deployment and needs Kubernetes 1.30 or later. Pick one of the methods below; all of them install the same signed image from ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-resource-operator.

HelmManifestOperatorHub 
helm install harbor-resource-operator oci://ghcr.io/oreondev/charts/harbor-resource-operator \
  --version 0.1.6 \
  --namespace harbor-resource-operator-system --create-namespace

Useful values:

Value Default Meaning manager.args [--leader-elect] Manager flags; add --watch-namespaces=a,b to restrict the operator to some namespaces manager.replicas 1 More replicas wait as hot standbys (leader election) crd.keep true Keep the CRDs, and so your objects, on helm uninstall metrics.enabled true Serve /metrics on port 8443 (HTTPS, authenticated) prometheus.enabled false Create a ServiceMonitor (needs the Prometheus operator) networkPolicy.enabled false Restrict ingress to the manager 
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/oreondev/harbor-resource-operator/releases/download/v0.1.6/install.yaml

This installs the CRDs, RBAC and the manager into harbor-resource-operator-system.

The operator is listed on OperatorHub.io. With OLM installed:

kubectl create -f https://operatorhub.io/install/harbor-resource-operator.yaml

OLM then upgrades the operator when a new version is published.

docs.title: Verify the image
docs.text:
Images are signed with cosign (keyless) by the release workflow, and carry an SBOM and provenance:

cosign verify ghcr.io/oreondev/harbor-resource-operator:0.1.6 \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/oreondev/harbor-resource-operator/' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: Upgrade with helm upgrade, by applying the newer install.yaml, or let OLM do it. Objects keep their Harbor IDs across upgrades; the operator finds what it created by the stored ID first.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Delete your Harbor resources first if you want their deletionPolicy to run; otherwise the finalizers keep them until the operator is back. Then:

helm uninstall harbor-resource-operator --namespace harbor-resource-operator-system

With crd.keep: true the CRDs and your objects stay in the cluster; nothing is deleted in Harbor.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The manager serves Prometheus metrics on port 8443 over HTTPS; scraping needs a token with access to the /metrics non-resource URL. With the Helm chart, prometheus.enabled: true creates a ServiceMonitor.

Besides the controller-runtime reconcile metrics, the operator exports:

Metric Labels Meaning harbor_api_requests_total connection, method, code Requests to Harbor by status code harbor_api_request_duration_seconds connection, method Harbor API latency harbor_drift_corrections_total kind Values restored after a change in Harbor harbor_resources kind, connection, ready Managed resources by readiness harbor_robot_expiration_timestamp_seconds namespace, name, robot When each robot account expires

docs.title: Example alerts
docs.text:
- alert: HarborRobotExpiresSoon
  expr: harbor_robot_expiration_timestamp_seconds - time() < 7 * 86400
  labels: { severity: warning }
  annotations:
    summary: "Robot {{ $labels.robot }} expires within a week"
- alert: HarborResourcesNotReady
  expr: sum by (kind, connection) (harbor_resources{ready="false"}) > 0
  for: 30m
  labels: { severity: warning }

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This takes about five minutes on any cluster where the operator is installed and that can reach your Harbor.

docs.title: 1. Connect a Harbor
docs.text:
Store the credentials in a Secret, in a namespace only the platform team can read, and point a HarborConnection at Harbor:

kubectl create namespace harbor-system
kubectl -n harbor-system create secret generic prod-harbor-admin \
  --from-literal=username='<harbor user>' --from-literal=password='<password>'

apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborConnection
metadata:
  name: prod-harbor
  namespace: harbor-system
spec:
  url: https://harbor.example.com
  credentialsSecretRef:
    name: prod-harbor-admin
  allowedNamespaces: ["*"]   # namespaces whose resources may use this connection

kubectl -n harbor-system get hconn

The connection becomes Ready once Harbor accepts the credentials. If Harbor uses a private CA, set caBundleSecretRef; see the HarborConnection reference.

Which Harbor account?

System-level kinds (projects, registries, replication, global labels, garbage collection, system robots) need a Harbor administrator or a system robot account with those permissions. The end-to-end suite runs as an administrator; a least-privilege robot setup is not verified yet.

docs.title: 2. Create a project and a robot account
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborProject
metadata:
  name: team-payments
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef: { name: prod-harbor, namespace: harbor-system }
  name: payments
  storageQuotaBytes: 53687091200   # 50 GiB
  metadata:
    autoScan: true
    preventVulnerable: true
    severity: critical
---
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborRobotAccount
metadata:
  name: payments-ci
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef: { name: prod-harbor, namespace: harbor-system }
  name: ci
  level: project
  projectRef: { name: team-payments }
  duration: 90
  permissions:
  - access:
    - { resource: repository, action: push }
    - { resource: repository, action: pull }
  secret:
    name: payments-ci-regcred
    type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
  rotation:
    beforeExpiry: 168h

kubectl create namespace team-payments
kubectl apply -f project-and-robot.yaml
kubectl -n team-payments get hproj,hrobot

Both objects show their Harbor ID and Ready=True within seconds. The robot's credentials are in the Secret payments-ci-regcred, ready for imagePullSecrets or a CI job, and the operator recreates the robot a week before it expires.

docs.title: 3. Watch drift correction
docs.text:
Change the project's severity in the Harbor UI and wait for the sync period (10 minutes by default, syncPeriod on the connection or the resource). The operator puts it back and records an event:

kubectl -n team-payments get events --field-selector reason=DriftCorrected

docs.title: HarborConnection
docs.text:
HarborConnection points the operator at one Harbor instance and the credentials to use.

API version harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1, namespaced, short name hconn.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: prod-harbor-admin
  namespace: harbor-system
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: admin                   # or a system robot with permissions for the kinds you use
  password: change-me
---
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborConnection
metadata:
  name: prod-harbor
  namespace: harbor-system
spec:
  url: https://harbor.example.com
  credentialsSecretRef:
    name: prod-harbor-admin
  allowedNamespaces: ["*"]
  syncPeriod: 10m

docs.title: Spec
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Description allowedNamespaces []string allowedNamespaces lists namespaces whose resources may reference this connection. "*" allows every namespace. The connection's own namespace is always allowed. caBundleSecretRef object caBundleSecretRef names a Secret in this namespace with key "ca.crt" holding PEM certificates to trust for the Harbor URL. caBundleSecretRef.name string yes name of the referenced object. credentialsSecretRef object yes credentialsSecretRef names a Secret in this namespace with keys "username" and "password". Use a system robot account with the permissions the operator needs rather than the admin user. credentialsSecretRef.name string yes name of the referenced object. insecureSkipTLSVerify boolean insecureSkipTLSVerify disables TLS certificate verification. Not for production. requestsPerSecond int32 10 requestsPerSecond caps the request rate the operator sends to this Harbor. syncPeriod string 10m syncPeriod is the default interval at which resources using this connection are re-read from Harbor and drift is corrected. url string yes url of the Harbor instance, for example https://harbor.example.com. The API path /api/v2.0 is appended by the operator.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Description conditions []object conditions: Ready=True when Harbor answered with the expected credentials. harborVersion string harborVersion reported by GET /systemInfo. lastCheckTime date-time lastCheckTime is when the connection was last verified. observedGeneration int64 observedGeneration is the spec generation the status reflects. username string username the operator authenticated as.

docs.title: HarborGarbageCollection
docs.text:
HarborGarbageCollection manages Harbor's garbage collection schedule.

API version harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1, namespaced, short name hgc.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborGarbageCollection
metadata:
  name: harbor-gc
  namespace: harbor-system
spec:
  connectionRef:
    name: prod-harbor
    namespace: harbor-system
  # Hourly, Daily, Weekly, None, or a six-field cron.
  schedule: "0 0 4 * * 0"
  deleteUntagged: true
  workers: 2
  # Retain leaves the schedule in Harbor when this object is deleted.
  deletionPolicy: Retain

docs.title: Spec
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Description connectionRef object yes connectionRef selects the Harbor instance. Needs a system administrator connection. connectionRef.name string yes name of the HarborConnection. connectionRef.namespace string namespace of the HarborConnection. Defaults to the namespace of the referencing resource. A cross-namespace reference is only honoured when the connection's spec.allowedNamespaces permits it. deleteUntagged boolean deleteUntagged also deletes untagged artifacts. deletionPolicy Retain \ Delete Retain schedule string yes schedule is Hourly, Daily, Weekly, None, or a six-field cron expression (seconds first) such as "0 0 3 * * 6". syncPeriod string syncPeriod overrides the connection's drift-correction interval. workers int32 1 workers run garbage collection in parallel, 1 to 5.

docs.title: HarborImmutableRule
docs.text:
HarborImmutableRule manages a tag immutability rule in a Harbor project.

API version harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1, namespaced, short name himmutable.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborImmutableRule
metadata:
  name: release-tags
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef:
    name: prod-harbor
    namespace: harbor-system
  projectRef:
    name: team-payments
  # Tags matching v*.*.* in every repository can never be overwritten.
  repositories:
    pattern: "**"
  tags:
    decoration: matches
    pattern: "v*.*.*"

docs.title: HarborProject
docs.text:
HarborProject manages a Harbor project: visibility, storage quota, scanning, CVE allowlist and proxy cache.

API version harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1, namespaced, short name hproj.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborProject
metadata:
  name: team-payments
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef:
    name: prod-harbor
    namespace: harbor-system
  name: payments
  public: false
  storageQuotaBytes: 53687091200
  metadata:
    autoScan: true
    preventVulnerable: true
    severity: critical
    reuseSystemCVEAllowlist: true
  deletionPolicy: Retain

docs.title: HarborRetentionPolicy
docs.text:
HarborRetentionPolicy manages the tag retention policy of a Harbor project.

API version harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1, namespaced, short name hretention.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: harbor.oreonit.com/v1alpha1
kind: HarborRetentionPolicy
metadata:
  name: payments-retention
  namespace: team-payments
spec:
  connectionRef:
    name: prod-harbor
    namespace: harbor-system
  projectRef:
    name: team-payments
  # Harbor keeps an artifact if any rule retains it.
  rules:
  - template: latestPushedK
    count: 10
    repositories:
      pattern: "**"
    tags:
      pattern: "**"
      untagged: false
  - template: always
    tags:
      pattern: "v*.*.*"
  # Six-field cron (seconds first), as Harbor expects. Empty means manual only.
  schedule: "0 0 3 * * *"

  connectionRef:

    namespace: harbor-system

  level: project

    name: team-payments

  duration: 90
  permissions:
  - access:
    - { resource: repository, action: push }
    - { resource: repository, action: pull }
    - { resource: artifact, action: read }

    name: payments-ci-regcred
    type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

    beforeExpiry: 168h
